title: Frugal Edge: continuous batching advisor with KV-aware heuristics
creator: Avery Sinclair
description: Build an automated recommendation engine that synthesizes continuous workload profiles, KV-cache awareness, and conservative heuristics to propose safe batching/caching configuration changes. The goal is to reduce per-token inference cost across mixed workloads while preserving tail latency SLOs. This ticket covers the core recommender: workload signal collection, feature engineering, heuristic rule-set, candidate generator, and a shadow/preview safe-apply pipeline that produces human-reviewable rollouts and automatic rollback triggers.
motivation: Current batching tuning is manual and reactive. Engineering spends large time iterating on configs for individual tenants and model families. We need an automated advisor that suggests low-risk, high-value changes and supports gradual rollouts with clear rollback criteria to avoid regressions in p99 latency and error rates.
success_metrics: reduce avg cost-per-token by >= 6% for targeted workloads within 6 weeks of rollout
no increase in p99 latency greater than 5% for recommended applies across canary cohorts
automated rollback triggers fire and revert changes within 2 minutes when thresholds breached
>75% of recommended changes accepted by SRE/PM after shadow evaluation
acceptance_criteria: service collects per-route and per-model workload signatures (sequence length distribution, arrival inter-arrival times, KV hit ratio) with low overhead (<0.5% CPU)
candidate generator outputs deterministic batching+cache config proposals with rationale and estimated cost delta
shadow pipeline runs proposals for 24h and produces a report: latency deltas (p50/p95/p99), error rate, cost estimate, and safety score
rollout API supports: preview, staged canary (traffic %, cohort), auto-monitoring, automatic rollback on defined thresholds
UI/CLI exposes proposal details and links to experiment dashboard and PR template for human approval
tasks: instrument telemetry: per-request sequence_len, kv_lookup_count, kv_hit, arrival_ts (ENG-1)
implement workload fingerprinting job: hourly aggregation into compact signature store (ENG-2)
design heuristic ruleset + scoring function (cost_saved_estimate vs risk_score) (ENG-3)
candidate generator service: produce top-3 config proposals per route and explainable features (ENG-4)
shadow/preview runner: apply config in shadow on routing layer, collect metrics for 24h (ENG-5)
rollout controller: staged apply/monitor/rollback hooks with alerting (ENG-6)
integrate with Console: proposal visualization and approve button (ENG-7)
end-to-end tests and a safety-canary synthetic workload harness (ENG-8)
design_notes: Prefer lightweight signatures (histogram + simple quantiles) over raw traces to keep storage small
KV-aware rules: avoid increasing batch size for routes with high KV-miss rates unless cached prewarm likelihood > 60%
Use conservative default multipliers for burst-prone routes; allow more aggressive tuning on stable background workloads
Produce a textual rationale per proposal: e.g., 'Increase batch from 8->12 (estimated -7% cost) — KV hit ratio 82%, median seq_len 64, p99 arrival 230ms'
Safety score combines p99 latency delta expectation, error rate sensitivity, and traffic volatility metric
implementation_decisions: Store signatures in TimescaleDB for efficient time-windowed queries
Candidate generator runs as serverless job once per hour; proposals cached for 6 hours
Shadow runner leverages existing routing shadow mode; metrics emitted to new dashboard view
Automatic rollback will be implemented via rollback webhook that calls the rollout controller; threshold actions are opaque to downstream apps and revert config atomically
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive batching could spike p99 latency. Mitigation: require shadow evaluation and staged canary with tight p99 thresholds before full apply.
Risk: Telemetry overhead. Mitigation: sample 1% of low-traffic routes and full for >1 RPS routes; optimize collection in C++ hot path.
Risk: Incorrect cost model. Mitigation: calibrate estimator against observed spend in pilot tenants and include uncertainty bounds in recommendations.
